parts: Imagine a notebook shared by everyone in your apartment building.
Today, most records live with one keeper: a bank, a registry, a company.
If that one book is wrong, lost or quietly changed, you just have to trust them.
A blockchain is a shared notebook that thousands of computers keep at the same time.
New entries are grouped into pages called blocks.
Each page carries a fingerprint of the page before it, like links in a chain.
Change one old entry, and its fingerprint changes.
Every page after it breaks, and every other copy disagrees.
So before a new page is added, the computers must agree it's valid.
Bitcoin's chain has added a new block about every ten minutes since January, two thousand nine,
The catch: a blockchain only proves what was written.
If someone writes a lie, it becomes a permanent, well-recorded lie.
A blockchain doesn't make people honest.
It makes records very hard to quietly change.
Just like that notebook, when everyone holds a copy.
